messages:
maria: Quick convo — thinking about adding routing/quota metadata to saved queries so the console can show a live 'cost & route' preview before you save. e.g. show what model would be routed, sample burn impact, and fallback route if quota hits.

alex: big yes to preview. product teams always get surprised by model swaps in rollouts. need an explicit UX signal. :warning:

jordan: backend note: we currently store saved_query -> route_id and query_json. We don't persist 'routing intent' (like preferred_model_hint, max_cost_tier). Curious how we'd represent that in the API.

sarah: UX: two quick affordances — (1) compact preview pill: "Model: gpt-4o-small (canary)" + cost delta; (2) route fallback disclosure that expands to show priority list. Keep it unobtrusive.

maria: +1. Proposal: saved queries gain optional metadata: tags: [preferred_model, fallback_chain, cost_budget, sample_rate_preview]. API contract v2 would accept metadata on create/update.

alex: sample API sketch:```POST /api/v2/saved_queries
{
  "route_id":"r-123",
  "name":"Top routes - 7d",
  "query":{...},
  "routing_metadata":{
    "preferred_model_hint":"redwood/gpt-4o-small",
    "fallback_chain":["redwood/gpt-4o-small","redwood/gpt-4o-base"],
    "cost_budget_tokens":50000
  }
}
```

jordan: fine, but we must be careful: runtime routing policy is decoupled. API can carry hints, but the serving layer may still override for capacity. We need an 'effective-routing' endpoint that expands the hint into what will actually be used.

sarah: UX: show both "preferred" and "effective" in preview. Preferred = what user asked for. Effective = what console currently predicts. Add a timestamp + link to telemetry for why it chose that model.

sam: telemetry/metrics team: to support this we need a per-saved-query sampling id so previews and dashboards can tie real traffic to the saved query definitions. Otherwise attribution is messy.

maria: good call. add field preview_sample_id -> used only for telemetry correlation. also we should surface sampling rate and last-eval timestamp.

jordan: small API opt: GET /api/v2/saved_queries/:id?expand=preview,telemetry will return an object with strings only (no heavy arrays) and a short preview: { predicted_model, predicted_cost_per_1000_tokens, fallback_reason } so console doesn't call routing runtime for every hover.

alex: performance concern — if we try to compute predictions for many saved queries in a folder, we risk spamming the routing service. We should cache predictions and mark them stale after X minutes.

maria: agree — caching + a 'refresh preview' CTA. Defaults: cache TTL 5m for canary, 1m for stable.

sam: telemetry: also track "preview divergence" metric: predicted_model != actual_served_model for first N requests after save. Useful for rollouts.

sarah: and from UX POV, when divergence > threshold show a yellow badge and CTA "re-sync hint".

jordan: one more internal API debate — do we version routing_metadata shape as part of saved_query resource, or make a separate resource /saved_query_routing_hints? Separate resource might let platform admin only update routing hints without touching query body.

maria: let's do separate resource. Cleaner ACLs: product can edit query content, infra/ops can manage routing hints.

alex: agree. Also add RBAC: only allowed roles can add cost_budget or set fallback_chain.

sam: I'll add telemetry fields to the plan: preview_sample_id, last_preview_at, preview_ttl_seconds, divergence_count.

maria: next steps: jordan + sam to draft API v2 contract for /saved_queries and /saved_query_routing_hints; sarah to mock the compact preview pill and badge states; alex to add cache+rate limits for preview endpoints. We'll sync early next week. :calendar: 

ops-bot: Deploy note — feature-flag "saved-query-routing-preview" created, default off for prod.

maria: thanks — can we add a short acceptance criteria doc in the PR? I'll draft it.
